deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let pi be the fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,inf}, with generators l_0, l_1, l_inf satisfying l_0 l_1 l_inf = 1, and inertia classes L_0, L_1, L_inf. Let pi^ be its profinite completion.

The large groups.
- Gamma^^ = Autext_loc(pi^) is the group of outer automorphisms preserving the set of inertia classes up to a common exponent p in Z^*. It is Z^* x S_3.
- E^^ is its inverse image in Aut(pi^).
- SE^^ is the group of 'rectified' automorphisms. Its elements are tuples (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_inf) with u(l_i) = g_i l_{sigma(i)}^p g_i^{-1}.
- Pi x Z^{0,1,inf} acts by i(g, alpha), since each g_i is only defined up to powers of l_{sigma(i)}. These are formulas (8)-(10) of the previous pages.

This page. Grothendieck restricts to the discrete part SE, the inverse image of Gamma = S_3 x Z/2 = S_3 x {±1} in Gamma^^. He looks at specific lifts:
- rho-dot, for the 3-cycle;
- sigma_i, for the transposition fixing i;
- tau_i, generating the stabilizers of the cusp i.

He already had a multiplicative lift into E of Gamma_p^* = {(sigma, sgn(sigma))}, a copy of S_3 inside S_3 x Z/2, given by rho-dot -> rho and sigma_0-dot -> sigma_0 tau_0. He also had lifts of the cusp stabilizers. He now lifts Gamma_p^* to a canonical homomorphism (11), rho: Gamma_p^* -> SE, a partial section of SE -> Gamma. It is given by (12):
- rho-dot |-> (1, rho, 1, 1, 1);
- sigma_i' = (sigma_i, -1) |-> (-1, sigma_i, 1, 1, 1).
All rectifiers are trivial.

Check.
- The 3-cycle l_0 -> l_1 -> l_inf -> l_0 preserves the relation, since l_1 l_inf l_0 is a cyclic conjugate of l_0 l_1 l_inf.
- A transposition reverses the cyclic order, so it must be paired with p = -1. For example l_0 -> l_1^{-1}, l_1 -> l_0^{-1} sends l_0 l_1 to l_1^{-1} l_0^{-1} = l_inf, hence l_inf -> l_inf^{-1}.

He then begins to say that the set of (p, sigma, g) with all g_i = 1 is a subgroup. The next page characterizes it by (13), l_{sigma0}^p l_{sigma1}^p l_{sigma inf}^p = 1. In the discrete case this gives exactly Gamma_p.

Purpose. This belongs to the 'Longue Marche' / Teichmüller-tower programme of 1981. Rigidified ('rectified') automorphisms of the profinite tripod group, with tangential-type normalizations, are an avatar of what Drinfeld/Ihara later formalized as GT^ (sigma(x) = x^lambda, sigma(y) = f^{-1} y^lambda f). The page isolates the S_3 x {±1} symmetries (anharmonic group composed with complex conjugation/orientation reversal) as an honest group of automorphisms with trivial rectifiers.
errors: Notational slips. The page alternates between Gamma^+, Gamma_p^* and Gamma_p for the same subgroup {(sigma, sg sigma)}. In (12), the target writes sigma-dot_i where sigma_i is meant.

Minor concern (next page, not this one). The relation as written in (14), l_inf^p l_1^p l_0^p = 1, holds for p = -1 rather than p = 1, since (l_0 l_1 l_inf)^{-1} = 1. The parenthetical 'quitte à corriger par un sigma~_i' presumably intends the cyclically ordered version l_0^p l_1^p l_inf^p = 1 => p = 1.

ideas.what: Rectified automorphisms (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_inf) of the profinite tripod group: automorphisms together with chosen conjugators sending each inertia generator to a conjugate of a p-th power of a permuted inertia generator
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving ('special', braid-like) automorphisms with tangential normalization; precursor of the GT^ parametrization (lambda, f)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 (GT^); Ihara (Galois action on pi_1(P^1-3pts)); Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); La Longue Marche (1981, circulated, partly edited by Schneps)

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphic section rho: Gamma_p^* ≅ S_3 -> SE with trivial rectifiers: 3-cycles with p = 1, transpositions paired with p = -1
ideas.modern_name: S_3 (anharmonic) symmetry of the tripod combined with complex conjugation; the elements theta, omega and the conjugation (-1, 1) of GT^

ideas.what: The rectified automorphisms with all g_i = 1 form a subgroup characterized by l_{sigma0}^p l_{sigma1}^p l_{sigma inf}^p = 1

missed.claim: On the following page Grothendieck leaves as 'Exercice!' the question whether, in the profinite free group, x^p y^p z^p = 1 (with xyz = 1, p in Z^*) forces p = ±1, i.e. whether the trivially-rectified part of SE^^ equals the discrete one. This amounts to determining the elements of GT^ with f = 1, which are generally understood to be (±1, 1). So it is not new, but it shows Grothendieck isolating this question in 1981.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld rigidified description of the Teichmüller-tower symmetry group; historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine computation within the known 1981 Longue Marche programme. The S_3 x {±1} lift with trivial rectifiers is standard in later GT^ literature. The historical interest lies in the pre-GT^ formalism, not in any new result.
transcription_corrections: Gamma is S_3 x Z/2, not S_3 x Z/12; the next page confirms {±1} x S_3 ≅ S_3 x Z_2 ≅ Gamma.
'Autext π̂^loc' is more likely 'Autext_loc π̂', with 'loc' written as a subscript.
The struck word before 'CNB' is probably '(notations' rather than 'relevant', i.e. '(notations CNB; ils sont vus dans E)'.
The first element is rho-dot (ρ̇), not ρ̃.
The definitions in (12) read ρ̃ and σ̃_i'.
